A React ref prop. The part exposes `validate()`, and the case "validates the field when the `validate` method is called" tests it. `pnpm parity:check` cannot read that member, because vue-component-meta leaves out an exposed member that has the name of a prop, and `validate` is also a prop.

The row gives the default `'onSubmit'`. The part has no Vue default: a prop that is absent takes the `validationMode` of the form, and `'onSubmit'` with no form, as in Base UI. With a Vue default, the part cannot find out that the prop is absent.

surfaceAdditions.reason: The part reads `value` to find out that it is controlled, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the input, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.
The part has the prop `value`, so `v-model:value` needs this emit. `types.md` has no row `value`, so the check expects no such emit.
The part gives `id` to the labelable provider and follows a change of it, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the input.
The part registers `name` with the field and follows a change of it, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the input.
The part reads `disabled` for the state and for the registration, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the input.
The part gives `id` to the labelable provider as the id of a message and follows a change of it, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the div.
